claims.claim: The best-performing agent (OpenAI o1-preview with AIDE scaffolding) achieves at least a Kaggle bronze medal in 16.9% of MLE-bench competitions.
claims.quote: best-performing setup--OpenAI's o1-preview with AIDE scaffolding--achieves at least the level of a Kaggle bronze medal in 16.9% of competitions.

claims.claim: A Claude v3 Opus agent achieves a 37.5% average success rate across MLAgentBench tasks.
claims.quote: It can build compelling ML models over many tasks in MLAgentBench with 37.5% average success rate.

claims.claim: Success rates for LLM agents on MLAgentBench vary from 100% on older datasets to 0% on recent Kaggle challenges.
claims.quote: success rates vary considerably; they span from 100% on well-established older datasets to as low as 0% on recent Kaggle challenges created potentially after the underlying LM was trained.

claims.claim: An optimized search strategy and operator set increases the Kaggle medal success rate on MLE-bench Lite from 39.6% to 47.7%.
claims.quote: Our best pairing of search strategy and operator set achieves a state-of-the-art result on MLE-bench lite, increasing the success rate of achieving a Kaggle medal from 39.6% to 47.7%.

claims.claim: MLE-STAR achieves medals in 64% of Kaggle competitions on MLE-bench Lite.
claims.quote: MLE-STAR achieves medals in 64% of the Kaggle competitions on the MLE-bench Lite, significantly outperforming the best alternative.

open_questions: How do success rates compare across different agent scaffolds and LLM backbones beyond those tested?
What are the failure modes for agents on recent Kaggle challenges that postdate LLM training data?
How well do these benchmarks predict performance on open-ended, novel ML research problems?
What is the success rate of smaller open-source models (e.g., 7B) on MLE-bench or MLAgentBench?
How do iterative debugging and long-horizon planning affect success rates in interactive environments like MLE-Dojo?
